verdicts.quote: For a connected app to request access, it must be integrated with the Salesforce API using the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
verdicts.reason: Salesforce integrations authenticate via OAuth 2.0 through Connected Apps/External Client Apps, which is the standard flow a multi-tenant agent would use.

verdicts.quote: Start building on Salesforce for free... Developer Edition.
verdicts.reason: Anyone can self-serve a free Developer Edition org and obtain OAuth credentials (now via External Client Apps) without contacting sales.

verdicts.quote: other Salesforce APIs, such as Bulk 2.0 API, Metadata API, and Connect REST API, offer additional functionality...
verdicts.reason: Salesforce provides many APIs across data, metadata, events, and tooling (REST, SOAP, Bulk 2.0, Metadata, Tooling, Pub/Sub, CDC), indicating broad coverage.

verdicts.quote: Salesforce MCP Servers connect your AI tools and agents to Salesforce data, metadata, and actions through the open Model Context Protocol (MCP).
verdicts.reason: MCP servers and guides are published and maintained by Salesforce, with hosted servers GA.

verdicts.quote: Not all Salesforce editions include API access... [Enterprise, Unlimited, Developer, Performance] include API access by default... Professional... can be purchased as an add-on.
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable now, but real orgs may lack API access on some editions and are subject to org admin controls and API limits, so caveats apply.
